initial_prompt: Use case: restrained editorial aviation illustration. Original 3:2 landscape blog cover, 1536x1024. A complete fictional modest two-seat high-wing piston training airplane with fixed tricycle landing gear and a simple two-blade propeller is parked on a quiet small-airport apron just outside an open plain hangar. View from elevated front-left three-quarter angle, whole airplane including both wingtips and tail visible with generous clear margins at every image edge. The airplane is the clear main subject, taking about two thirds of the frame width; pale cream fuselage, muted slate-blue trim, coherent wings and struts. Farther behind near the hangar, two very small anonymous figures stand beside one closed flight bag, suggesting a student and instructor preparing for a lesson; people remain secondary and have no identifiable faces. A second distant trainer parked near the hangar provides subtle context, not a comparison diagram. Calm morning light, simplified graphic forms, slightly abstract magazine illustration, controlled cream, blue and warm-grey palette and subtle paper texture. No flying, no dramatic action, no cockpit detail, no clutter. Absolutely no text: no titles, letters, numbers, registrations, labels, logos, signage, arrows, badges or watermarks. Fictional editorial illustration, not a photograph of a plane for sale.
refinement_prompt: Refine only the framing of this aviation editorial illustration. Zoom the scene out by about 20 percent while preserving the same complete high-wing training airplane, hangar, tiny student/instructor figures, quiet atmosphere, coherent aircraft geometry, cream and blue palette and graphic illustration style. The main airplane must be entirely inside the 3:2 image with at least 8 percent empty clearance from BOTH wing tips to the image edges; the main right wing tip must move well away from the right edge. Keep the people small and secondary. No text, numbers, logos, registrations, watermarks or new objects. Keep a 3:2 landscape composition.
